questions.question: What type of content can S3 Static Website Hosting serve?

explanation.correct: S3 Static Website Hosting serves static files — HTML, CSS, JS, and images. No server-side execution.
explanation.why: A and C require compute/database services. D requires container services like ECS.

questions.question: Which AWS service is Amazon's Content Delivery Network (CDN)?

explanation.correct: CloudFront is AWS's CDN service, caching content at edge locations globally.
explanation.why: Route 53 is DNS. ELB distributes traffic between servers. Global Accelerator optimises routing but is not a CDN.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Origin Access Control (OAC) in CloudFront?

options.text: To allow all internet users to access S3 directly
To restrict S3 bucket access so only a specific CloudFront distribution can read it
To encrypt data at rest in S3

explanation.correct: OAC keeps the S3 bucket private — only the specific CloudFront distribution with the correct ID is permitted to read the bucket.
explanation.why: A is the opposite of OAC's purpose. C is handled by S3 encryption settings. D is a CloudFront compression feature.

questions.question: What is a CloudFront Distribution domain name?

options.text: The S3 static website endpoint URL
A URL like dxxxxx.cloudfront.net assigned to your CloudFront distribution
Your Route 53 hosted zone name servers

explanation.correct: After creating a distribution, CloudFront assigns a domain name in the format dxxxxx.cloudfront.net which customers use to access content.
explanation.why: The S3 endpoint is the origin URL. Route 53 name servers are for DNS. EC2 has its own public DNS.

questions.question: What is Amazon Route 53?

explanation.correct: Route 53 is AWS's authoritative DNS service — it translates domain names into IP addresses and can route traffic using various policies.
explanation.why: Load balancing is ELB. CDN is CloudFront. Key-value database is DynamoDB or ElastiCache.

questions.question: What is a Route 53 hosted zone?

options.text: A container for DNS records for a specific domain

explanation.correct: A hosted zone in Route 53 is a container that holds DNS records (A records, CNAME, MX, etc.) for a specific domain.
explanation.why: Availability zones and subnets are network concepts. Edge locations are CloudFront infrastructure.

questions.question: What is Boto3?

options.text: The official AWS SDK for Python

explanation.correct: Boto3 is the official AWS SDK for Python, allowing developers to programmatically interact with AWS services from Python code.
explanation.why: CDN is CloudFront. Database migration uses AWS DMS. Boto3 is not a CLI plugin — it is a standalone library.

questions.question: What command configures AWS credentials for Boto3 use?

explanation.correct: 'aws configure' is the AWS CLI command that sets up the access key ID, secret access key, region, and output format used by both the CLI and Boto3.
explanation.why: boto3 configure and aws init are not valid commands. pip install aws installs a package but does not configure credentials.

questions.question: S3 bucket names must be:

options.text: Unique within a single AWS region
Globally unique across all AWS accounts

explanation.correct: S3 bucket names must be globally unique — no two buckets anywhere in the world (across all AWS accounts) can have the same name.
explanation.why: S3 is a global namespace service. Regional or account uniqueness is not sufficient.

questions.question: What is the default root object you typically set in a CloudFront distribution for a website?

explanation.correct: The conventional default root object for a website is index.html — the landing page that loads when users visit the root URL.
explanation.why: While any filename can technically be used, index.html is the web standard convention.

questions.question: After enabling OAC on CloudFront, what happens when a user tries to access the S3 static website endpoint URL directly?

options.text: The user is redirected to CloudFront
The user receives a 403 Forbidden error
The bucket policy is removed automatically

explanation.correct: With Block Public Access enabled and only the OAC bucket policy in place, direct S3 access returns 403 Forbidden. Only CloudFront can access the bucket.
explanation.why: S3 does not redirect to CloudFront — it simply rejects the request. The bucket policy is not removed.

questions.question: What is the default TTL for cached objects in CloudFront?

explanation.correct: CloudFront's default TTL is 24 hours (86,400 seconds). Objects are cached at edge locations for this duration before CloudFront re-checks the origin.
explanation.why: The other values are not the default CloudFront TTL. TTL can be customised, but 24 hours is the default.

questions.question: What is a CloudFront cache hit?

options.text: When CloudFront fetches the object from the origin
When the object is found in the edge location cache and returned to the user without contacting the origin
When CloudFront blocks a malicious request
When the TTL expires and the cache is refreshed

explanation.correct: A cache hit occurs when the requested file is already cached at the edge location — it is served immediately without contacting S3, resulting in very low latency.
explanation.why: A describes a cache miss. C describes WAF. D describes cache expiry.

questions.question: Which Route 53 record type is recommended for pointing a domain to a CloudFront distribution?

explanation.correct: AWS recommends ALIAS records for CloudFront integration. ALIAS records work at the zone apex, are free for AWS resources, and resolve at the DNS level.
explanation.why: MX is for email. CNAME cannot be used at the zone apex (e.g., example.com). SOA is a zone metadata record.

questions.question: How many name servers does Route 53 assign when you create a hosted zone?

explanation.correct: Route 53 assigns exactly 4 name servers to each hosted zone for redundancy and availability.
explanation.why: Using 4 name servers ensures that DNS queries can be resolved even if some name servers are unreachable.

questions.question: What is the difference between boto3.resource() and boto3.client()?

options.text: resource() is for S3 only; client() is for EC2 only
resource() provides a high-level object-oriented API; client() provides low-level direct API calls
resource() is free; client() incurs charges
resource() uses REST; client() uses GraphQL

explanation.correct: boto3.resource() gives a higher-level, object-oriented interface. boto3.client() gives lower-level direct API access with full parameter control. Both can interact with the same services.
explanation.why: Both work with all supported services. AWS charges are based on API calls, not SDK method choice.

questions.question: AMI IDs in AWS are:

options.text: Region-specific — the same OS has a different AMI ID in each region
Account-specific — different for each AWS account

explanation.correct: AMI IDs are region-specific. The same Ubuntu image has a different AMI ID in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) vs us-east-1 (N. Virginia). Always look up the correct AMI ID for your target region.
explanation.why: AMIs are not account-specific for public AMIs. They are not automatically deprecated after a fixed period.

questions.question: Which AWS service is the only one that can register domain names?

explanation.correct: Route 53 is the only AWS service that can register domain names directly. All other services require you to already own a domain.
explanation.why: CloudFront, S3, and IAM do not have domain registration capabilities.

questions.question: A user uploads new content to S3 but CloudFront keeps serving the old version. What is the correct solution?

options.text: Delete and recreate the CloudFront distribution
Create a CloudFront Invalidation for the updated files
Disable and re-enable static website hosting

explanation.correct: A CloudFront Invalidation clears specific files from edge caches before their TTL expires, forcing CloudFront to fetch the latest version from S3 on the next request.
explanation.why: Recreating the distribution is unnecessary and slow. Region changes do not clear cache. Static website hosting has no effect on CloudFront cache.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid Route 53 routing policy?

explanation.correct: Throughput is not a Route 53 routing policy. The valid policies are Simple, Weighted, Latency, Failover, Geolocation, Geoproximity, and Multi-value Answer.
explanation.why: Weighted distributes by percentage, Latency routes to lowest-latency region, Failover switches to backup on health check failure.

questions.question: What happens to a CloudFront distribution when it is first created?

options.text: It is immediately available at all edge locations
It takes 5–20 minutes to deploy as settings propagate to all global edge locations
It requires manual activation in each region
It is only active in the origin region until manually expanded

explanation.correct: CloudFront distributions take 5–20 minutes to deploy because the configuration must propagate to all 400+ edge locations worldwide.
explanation.why: CloudFront automatically propagates globally — no manual region activation is needed.

questions.question: A company wants to route 10% of traffic to a new application version and 90% to the existing version for testing. Which Route 53 routing policy should they use?

explanation.correct: Weighted routing allows you to assign percentage weights to records, making it ideal for A/B testing and gradual deployments.
explanation.why: Latency routes by speed, Failover by health, Geolocation by user location — none of these control traffic percentages.

questions.question: In Boto3, what does instance.wait_until_running() do?

options.text: Pauses script execution until the instance state changes to 'running'
Checks if the instance type is available
Sends a health check request to the instance

explanation.correct: wait_until_running() is a Boto3 waiter that polls the EC2 API repeatedly until the instance reaches the 'running' state, then returns control to the script.
explanation.why: Termination uses terminate(). Instance type availability is checked separately. Health checks are separate from state polling.

questions.question: What is the advantage of ALIAS records over CNAME records in Route 53?

options.text: ALIAS records support more DNS record types
ALIAS records work at the zone apex and are free for AWS resources; CNAME records cannot be used at the zone apex
ALIAS records are faster than CNAME records
CNAME records cannot point to CloudFront

explanation.correct: The key advantages of ALIAS records are: they work at the zone apex (e.g., example.com without www), they are free of charge when pointing to AWS resources, and they resolve at the DNS level.
explanation.why: CNAME records cannot be created at the zone apex — this is a DNS specification limitation.

questions.question: Which architecture best solves both the latency problem and the S3 security concern for global website delivery?

options.text: Public S3 bucket in every region
Private S3 bucket + CloudFront with OAC + Route 53

explanation.correct: Private S3 (keeps bucket secure) + CloudFront with OAC (caches globally, enforces private access) + Route 53 (friendly domain mapping) is the standard production architecture for global static website delivery.
explanation.why: Multiple public S3 buckets is complex and insecure. Multiple EC2 instances are expensive and complex for static content. S3 Transfer Acceleration only speeds uploads to S3, not delivery to end users.

questions.question: A developer writes a Boto3 script in Mumbai that works correctly. The same script fails in Singapore with 'AMI not found'. What is the most likely fix?

options.text: Update the AMI ID to the correct ID for the ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) region

explanation.correct: AMI IDs are region-specific. The Mumbai AMI ID does not exist in Singapore. The developer must find the correct AMI ID for ap-southeast-1 and update the script.
explanation.why: Reinstalling Boto3 or changing instance types will not resolve a region-specific AMI ID mismatch.

questions.question: You want to ensure that users in Europe are always served by a CloudFront distribution backed by an S3 bucket in Frankfurt, while users in Asia are served by a distribution backed by Singapore. Which Route 53 routing policy would you use?

explanation.correct: Geolocation routing directs traffic based on the geographic location of the user. European users go to the Frankfurt CloudFront distribution; Asian users go to the Singapore one.
explanation.why: Weighted is percentage-based, Failover is for high availability, Simple returns a single value.

questions.question: What is the correct order to set up the S3 + CloudFront + Route 53 architecture?

options.text: S3 (create + upload) → CloudFront (create + OAC policy) → Route 53 (hosted zone + ALIAS record)
All three can be created simultaneously in any order

explanation.correct: You must create S3 and upload files first (origin must exist before CloudFront), then create CloudFront and apply the OAC bucket policy (distribution ID needed for policy), then configure Route 53 (CloudFront domain name needed for ALIAS record).
explanation.why: Each step depends on outputs from the previous step — the order matters.

questions.question: A company has two S3 buckets: one primary in us-east-1 and one backup in eu-west-1. They want traffic to automatically switch to the backup if the primary becomes unavailable. Which Route 53 routing policy should they use?

explanation.correct: Failover routing policy checks the health of the primary resource and automatically routes traffic to the secondary (backup) resource if the primary health check fails.
explanation.why: Latency routes by speed, Weighted by percentage, Multi-value returns multiple records — none provide automatic failover based on health checks.

questions.question: A DevOps team needs to automatically launch 50 EC2 instances every night at midnight for batch processing and terminate them at 6am. Which access method is MOST appropriate?

options.text: AWS Console — navigate and click for each instance
AWS CLI — type commands interactively each time
AWS SDK (Boto3) — write a Python script triggered by a cron job or Lambda
Contact AWS support to schedule the instances

explanation.correct: AWS SDK (Boto3) is the correct choice for automation — write a Python script that launches and terminates instances programmatically, scheduled via cron or AWS Lambda. This is repeatable, scalable, and requires no human interaction.
explanation.why: Console requires manual clicks — not scalable for 50 instances nightly. CLI is better than console but still requires manual invocation or complex shell scripting. AWS support does not manage customer instances.
